To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a new approach to channel estimation and data demodulation in doubly selective channels.
the proposed superimposed training and DPS BEM based channel estimation scheme provides a viable solution to the channel estimation problem in doubly selective channels.
We propose a novel channel estimation and data transmission scheme for frequency selective channels.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following: (1) the design of a superimposed training based channel estimation and detection system; (2) the design of the superimposed training sequences to achieve a good channel estimation performance while maintaining the integrity of the data; (3) the design of channel estimation algorithms that can be implemented in real time; and (4) the investigation of a maximum likelihood approach to enhance the performance of the system.
developing a novel superimposed training based channel estimation and data detector for frequency selective time-varying channels.
the design of a new class of superimposed training based channel estimation and data transmission techniques that are applicable to time varying frequency selective fading channels.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed approach is competitive with the conventional training scheme in terms of channel estimation performance.
the proposed approaches have the potential to provide significant improvements over the conventional TM training.
the proposed approach is a good candidate for high data rate wireless communication systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed superimposed training approach is a good compromise for the tradeoff between the data rate and the channel estimation performance.
the proposed superimposed training approach is a viable and attractive alternative to the conventional TM training.
the use of superimposed training and a discrete prolate basis expansion model for channel estimation and data recovery in doubly selective channels is a promising approach.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a PDD superimposition of training sequence with a suitable choice of design parameters can provide a good tradeoff between channel estimation and data rate.
the use of superimposed training and a DPS BEM can provide a viable solution for channel estimation and data demodulation for frequency selective time variant channels.
a superimposed training approach with DPS BEM can be used to achieve channel estimation with low SNIR and low complexity, and to improve the performance of channel estimation and data recovery.
